method: The conversion is a ratio, not an empirical model. Every length is parsed as a plain decimal number and converted to millimetres (1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 1000 mm, 1 in = 25.4 mm, 1 ft = 304.8 mm); the model length is the real length divided by the scale denominator N, and the real length is the model length multiplied by N, where the scale is written 1:N. For a model already in hand the denominator is recovered as N = real length / model length, and the page names the nearest common kit scale (1:12, 1:24, 1:32, 1:35, 1:48, 1:72, 1:76, 1:87, 1:144, 1:350) only when the recovered ratio lies within 15 % of it. The same ten scales are used for the table that repeats the real length as a model size, and the row matching the current scale is marked. Surface area scales with the square of the linear ratio and volume, and therefore mass at equal density, with the cube: a 1:72 model has 1/5184 of the surface and 1/373,248 of the volume of the object it represents. Inputs are accepted from 0.01 mm to 1,000,000 mm for a length and from 1 to 10,000 for the scale, with decimals allowed so a nominal scale such as the HO 1:87.1 can be entered; the model length is rejected when it is not shorter than the real length and the recovered ratio is rejected above 1:10,000. Results are shown to display precision and repeated in millimetres or inches, and the page only converts a length, so it says nothing about the proportions, weight or detail of a kit. Published kit scales are nominal: a moulding, a printed plan or a quoted model length is often a percent or two away from the label, and the two lengths must describe the same dimension (overall length against overall length, for example) for the ratio to mean anything. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
